messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] issue with streaming output from RStan?
parts:
I tested a very simple and I can see csv files are written incrementally during sampling.  In 1.2.0, write_csv function is used to write to the csv files, so 1.2.0 is not different from all previous versions in this respect.  

But I do see that after each iteration, there is not an explicite "flush" got called as in Stan.  I am not sure if an explicit "flush" after each iteration will help, but I will do that. 

I am not sure if I understood overwriting correctly.  But for csv files of sample in RStan, if the R process has the privilege to overwrite previous files, it will overwrite them. 


Jiqiang

parts:
I was just talking about this output:

> fit <- stan("normal_mixture_k.stan", iter=10000, data=c("K","N","y"), chains=1,fit=fit, init=0)
SAMPLING FOR MODEL 'normal_mixture_k' NOW (CHAIN 1).
Iteration: 1 / 10000 [ 0%] (Adapting)
Iteration: 1000 / 10000 [ 10%] (Adapting)
Iteration: 2000 / 10000 [ 20%] (Adapting)
Iteration: 3000 / 10000 [ 30%] (Adapting)
Iteration: 4000 / 10000 [ 40%] (Adapting)
Iteration: 5000 / 10000 [ 50%] (Adapting)
Iteration: 6000 / 10000 [ 60%] (Sampling)
Iteration: 7000 / 10000 [ 70%] (Sampling)
Iteration: 8000 / 10000 [ 80%] (Sampling)
Iteration: 9000 / 10000 [ 90%] (Sampling)
Iteration: 10000 / 10000 [100%] (Sampling)

>

After I hit return after calling stan(), I don't see anything
until all 10K iterations are done. So I don't know how fast
things are going.

What we'd like is to have the lines appear as soon as possible.

Usually in streaming I/O, there's a flush() operation to override
any buffering that might be done.

Andrew just wanted these lines to overwrite each other. At
which point, we can do them more frequently than just 10 total
updates.

- Bob

which point, we can do them more frequently than just 10 total
updates.
- Bob

> This is not the supposed behavior. At least using R from the command line, I have the similar behavior as in Stan;
> when another 10% iteration are done, it prints a line.
>
>
> What we'd like is to have the lines appear as soon as possible.
>
> Usually in streaming I/O, there's a flush() operation to override
> any buffering that might be done.
>
>
> The flush is already there. So I think if the progress percent does not get updated as the sampling goes, it is a
> bug with the R environment that is used.
>
>
> Andrew just wanted these lines to overwrite each other. At
> which point, we can do them more frequently than just 10 total
> updates.
>
>
> - Bob
